title: Johnny Richards waiting to take over
summary: Handy suspects they lined up Richards to replace him but does not blame Richards.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I was writing for the Raeburn band and I don't know who he was writing for. He was busy doing whatever he was doing.
By there--he wasn't on the Raeburn band? You mean he was in California?
Right. He was in the city, in the local; he was around.
So then "Rainbow" was the first time he touched the Raeburn band?
We may never solve that mystery.
I have a feeling that they were ready for me to leave and they had him ready to step in.
Why would the be ready for you to leave? Had there been an under-

I think they just had planned not to pay me according to the agreement and they were covering themselves in case I did decide to leave, and they might have been hoping that I would accept their way and I didn't, of course. But they covered themselves, because John was around for the last few weeks. He just happened to be in the club, around and I'm not a dummy. I'm sure that Boyd said, I think George is going to leave, how would you like to take over, because John--I remember him reassuring me, I'm not here for your job. I never said a word about why are you here. We were friends.
Did John ever play on the band?
He was alto playing, wasn't he?
Saxophone player, yes. I liked John; I didn't think he was a sneaky guy. In that particular situation I
think he got himself involved, he probably needed the money, needed the job and he wasn't doing anything wrong if I was going to leave.
